title: False hinge: grace need not hang on external signs — OT rites lacked NT sacramental force on Rome's own view
source_text: XVIII. Ad rem ipsam quod attinet dico, totam vim istius argumenti niti falsa quadam adversariorum hypothesi, nempe, quod gratia Dei necessario pendeat a signis quibusdam externis, quodque externus Sacramentorum actus vim habeat gratiam in nobis producendi. Hoc enim posito, mirum ipsis videtur qui potuerint foeminae salvari sub Veteri Testamento absque circumcisione, aut simili quopiam externo sacramento: Et tamen hac ipsa in re sui obliviscuntur. Nam quum de Sacramentis agunt, istam efficaciam & necessitatem tribuunt solis Sacramentis Novi Testamenti, non vero Sacramentis quae erant sub lege veteri, quae juxta ipsorum mentem erant tantum umbrae & figurae nostrorum, nec in se vim ullam habebant gratiam operandi. Ideoque si suis ipsorum placitis stare velint, neque circumcisio, nec ullus alius ritus sub Veteri Testamento potuit remedium esse peccati originalis.
pass_a_gloss: As to the matter itself I say that the whole force of that argument rests on a certain false hypothesis of the adversaries — namely, that the grace of God necessarily depends on certain external signs, and that the external act of the Sacraments has power to produce grace in us. For this being assumed, it seems wonderful to them how women could have been saved under the Old Testament without circumcision or some similar external sacrament: and yet in this very point they forget themselves. For when they treat of the Sacraments, they attribute that efficacy and necessity to the Sacraments of the New Testament alone, not to the Sacraments which were under the old law, which according to their mind were only shadows and figures of ours, and in themselves had no power of working grace. And therefore if they wish to stand by their own opinions, neither circumcision nor any other rite under the Old Testament could have been a remedy of original sin.
pass_b_english: The whole attack hangs on a false hinge: that grace must ride on outward signs.
On that hinge Rome wonders how women were saved without circumcision — yet she forgets her own teaching.
She grants New-Testament sacraments alone that grace-working force; Old-Testament rites she calls shadows without power to work grace.
Stand by that, and circumcision itself was no remedy of original sin.

lemmas.latin: gratia Dei necessario pendeat a signis

choices.why: Names the hinge before the reply.
Their own limit undercuts OT remedial claims.
